questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The University of Ibadan (UI) is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The University of Ibadan is located in Ibadan, the capital city of Oyo State.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In what year was the University of Ibadan founded, initially as University College Ibadan?
questions.explanation: The University College Ibadan (UCI) was established in 1948, making UI the first degree-awarding institution in Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: At its founding, University College Ibadan operated under a special academic relationship with which foreign university?
questions.explanation: UCI operated as a college in special relationship with the University of London, with its degrees initially awarded by that university before UI gained full university status.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In what year did University College Ibadan become a fully independent university able to award its own degrees?
questions.explanation: The University of Ibadan attained full university status in 1962, ending its earlier affiliation with the University of London.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: By what popular nickname is the University of Ibadan widely known among Nigerian universities?
questions.explanation: The University of Ibadan, as Nigeria's oldest university, is popularly nicknamed 'First and the Best'.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who is generally recognised as the first Nigerian Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan?
questions.explanation: Kenneth Onwuka Dike became the first Nigerian Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, serving in that role in the 1960s.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these celebrated writers studied at University College Ibadan in its early years?
questions.explanation: Both Wole Soyinka and Chinua Achebe were among the early students of University College Ibadan before it became a fully independent university.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Wole Soyinka, an alumnus of University College Ibadan, became the first African to win which major international prize?
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, becoming the first African laureate in that category.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The teaching hospital affiliated with the University of Ibadan's College of Medicine, and the first of its kind in Nigeria, is known as?
questions.explanation: University College Hospital (UCH) Ibadan, established in 1957, was Nigeria's first teaching hospital and remains affiliated with the University of Ibadan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Ibadan, the city that hosts the University of Ibadan, is often described in relation to other West African cities as?
options: One of the largest indigenous cities in West Africa
The smallest city in West Africa
A city with no historical significance
questions.explanation: Ibadan is widely described as one of the largest indigenous (pre-colonial, locally founded) cities in West Africa, with a long history predating British colonial rule.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Oyo State, where the University of Ibadan is situated, is officially given which nickname on its state emblem?
questions.explanation: Oyo State carries the official nickname 'Pacesetter State', reflecting its historical prominence as part of the former Western Region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Ibadan's older residential districts are sometimes described by which distinctive visual feature of their rooftops?
questions.explanation: Older parts of Ibadan are known for a dense spread of rusted, brown corrugated-iron roofing, a familiar sight when viewing the city from its hills.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Oyo State takes its name from which historic pre-colonial Yoruba empire?
questions.explanation: Oyo State derives its name from the Old Oyo Empire, one of the most powerful pre-colonial Yoruba states in West Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the traditional title of the paramount ruler of the Oyo Empire and its successor, the town of Oyo?
questions.explanation: The Alaafin of Oyo is the traditional royal title for the ruler of Oyo, historically the head of the powerful Oyo Empire.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The body responsible for accrediting academic programmes in Nigerian universities, including the University of Ibadan, is the?
questions.explanation: The NUC is the regulatory body responsible for approving and accrediting academic programmes offered by Nigerian universities, ensuring they meet minimum quality standards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which arm of government in Nigeria is primarily responsible for making laws?
questions.explanation: The Legislature (the National Assembly at federal level) is the arm of government responsible for making laws, distinct from the law-enforcing Executive and law-interpreting Judiciary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the Nigerian legislative chamber whose members represent an entire state, alongside the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: The Senate, together with the House of Representatives, forms Nigeria's bicameral National Assembly, with each state represented by three senators.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following countries shares a land border with Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria shares land borders with Cameroon, Niger, Chad, and Benin Republic; Ghana, South Africa, and Kenya are not bordering countries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the longest river in Africa?
questions.explanation: The Nile, flowing through north-eastern Africa, is the longest river on the continent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)?
options: Organising and supervising elections in Nigeria
questions.explanation: INEC is Nigeria's independent body responsible for organising, conducting, and supervising elections at the federal and state levels.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which cash crop was historically the dominant export of the old Western Region, which included present-day Oyo State?
questions.explanation: Cocoa was the dominant cash crop and export earner of the old Western Region of Nigeria, which included the area now forming Oyo State.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen's chemical symbol is simply 'O', as assigned on the periodic table of elements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Mars is nicknamed the 'Red Planet' because of the iron oxide (rust) prevalent on its surface, which gives it a reddish appearance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is Cameroon's national football team commonly nicknamed?
questions.explanation: Cameroon's senior men's national football team is popularly known as the Indomitable Lions, distinct from Nigeria's Super Eagles and Ghana's Black Stars.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which international body is primarily responsible for global public health coordination?
questions.explanation: The WHO is the United Nations agency specifically responsible for coordinating international public health matters.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a system of government headed by an elected president who is both head of state and head of government?
questions.explanation: In a presidential system, the president serves as both head of state and head of government, as is the case in Nigeria's current constitution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the Nigerian Customs Service?
options: Regulating and collecting duties on goods entering or leaving the country
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Customs Service is responsible for regulating the movement of goods across Nigeria's borders and collecting the associated duties and tariffs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a non-communicable disease?
questions.explanation: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is a non-communicable condition, unlike tuberculosis, cholera, and measles, which are infectious diseases.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the largest country in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Russia, spanning parts of both Europe and Asia, is the largest country in the world by total land area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who is generally credited with leading the Sokoto Jihad in the early 19th century, later founding the Sokoto Caliphate?
questions.explanation: Uthman Dan Fodio led the Sokoto Jihad in the early 19th century, a religious and political reform movement that resulted in the founding of the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary role of the judiciary in a democracy?
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets the law and administers justice, resolving disputes and checking the powers of the other arms of government.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which vitamin deficiency is most commonly associated with the disease rickets?
questions.explanation: Rickets, a condition causing weak or soft bones in children, is most commonly associated with a deficiency of Vitamin D.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the total value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens and businesses, regardless of location?
questions.explanation: GNP measures output produced by a country's nationals and businesses wherever they are located, unlike GDP which measures output within the country's borders.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What does the abbreviation 'NYSC' stand for in the Nigerian context?
questions.explanation: NYSC is the scheme requiring Nigerian graduates under a certain age to serve the nation for one year, often in a state other than their own.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a persistent, sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services in an economy?
questions.explanation: Inflation describes an ongoing, generalised increase in prices across an economy, reducing the purchasing power of money over time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary aim of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)?
options: Promoting economic integration and cooperation among West African countries
Restricting all trade between West African nations
questions.explanation: ECOWAS is a regional political and economic union of West African states aimed at promoting economic integration, free movement, and cooperation among member countries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a government budget in which planned revenue exceeds planned expenditure?
questions.explanation: A surplus budget occurs when a government's expected revenue exceeds its planned spending, the opposite of a deficit budget.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a key function of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) relating to monetary policy?
options: Setting the retail price of consumer goods
Regulating interest rates and the money supply
questions.explanation: One of the CBN's core functions is formulating and implementing monetary policy, including regulating interest rates and controlling the money supply.
